topic: Sheet Layout and Types of Drawing (IS 962 layout of drawing)
subtopic: Sheet Layout and Types of Drawing
question: The preferred size of the drawing sheets is recommended by the ______
explanation: Bureau of Indian Standards (B.I.S.), American Society of Mechanical Engineering (ASME), American Society for Testing and Materials (ASTM), U.S. National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST).
source: Engineering Drawing MCQs with explanations · p.7

subject: Engineering Drawing
topic: Sheet Layout and Types of Drawing (IS 962 layout of drawing)
subtopic: Sheet Layout and Types of Drawing
question: The untrimmed size for _______ sheet is 240 mm x 330 mm.
explanation: The untrimmed size of any sheet will be slightly larger than trimmed size. The untrimmed size for an A4 sheet is 240 mm x 330 mm where trimmed size is 210 mm x 297mm. The space between the trimmed sheet and the frame is called border.
source: Engineering Drawing MCQs with explanations · p.7

subject: Engineering Drawing
topic: Sheet Layout and Types of Drawing (IS 962 layout of drawing)
subtopic: Sheet Layout and Types of Drawing
question: SP: 46 (2003) recommends the borders of _______ mm width for the sheet sizes A0 and A1, and _______ mm for the sizes A2, A3, A4 and A5.
explanation: SP: 46 (2003) recommends the borders of 20 mm width for the sheet sizes A0 and A1, and 10 mm for the sizes A2, A3, A4 and A5. The BIS-SP 46 is the standard used in the educational institution for engineering drawing.
source: Engineering Drawing MCQs with explanations · p.7

subject: Engineering Drawing
topic: Sheet Layout and Types of Drawing (IS 962 layout of drawing)
subtopic: Sheet Layout and Types of Drawing
question: The false statement regarding orientation mark.
options: The orientation mark coincides with one of the centering marks
Represents the direction to which sheet is placed
Orientation mark can be used for the orientation of drawing sheet on the drawing board
Facilitate positioning of the drawing for reproduction purpose
explanation: The sheet may be placed in any direction but within the sheet, the drawing should be specified particularly for reproduction purpose, the main purpose is to facilitate positioning of the drawing and parts in it.
source: Engineering Drawing MCQs with explanations · p.8

subject: Engineering Drawing
topic: Sheet Layout and Types of Drawing (IS 962 layout of drawing)
subtopic: Sheet Layout and Types of Drawing
question: The size of the title block is ________ mm x ________ mm.
explanation: The size of the title block is 185mm x 65 mm which is recommended by B.I.S. (Bureau of Indian Standards), where 25mm x 10mm is for scale in drawing sheet. Within the title box there will be so many sections divided like Name of the firm, Drawing No, Title, etc.
source: Engineering Drawing MCQs with explanations · p.8

subject: Engineering Drawing
topic: Sheet Layout and Types of Drawing (IS 962 layout of drawing)
subtopic: Sheet Layout and Types of Drawing
question: The number of folding methods for folding of various sizes of drawing sheets is __________
explanation: The final size of the folded print in method 1 will be 297 x 190, while that in method 2 will be 297 x 210. In either case, the title block is visible at the top of the folded print. When prints are to be stored and preserved in cabinets they are folded by method 2.
source: Engineering Drawing MCQs with explanations · p.8

subject: Engineering Drawing
topic: Sheet Layout and Types of Drawing (IS 962 layout of drawing)
subtopic: Sheet Layout and Types of Drawing
question: Which of the following is reducing scale?
explanation: 0.5:1 is reducing scale which we can also be written as 1:2. In the remaining options the antecedent is more than the consequent. So we can say if antecedent is a decimal and consequent is whole number then the ratio is said to be reducing scale.
source: Engineering Drawing MCQs with explanations · p.8

subject: Engineering Drawing
topic: Sheet Layout and Types of Drawing (IS 962 layout of drawing)
subtopic: Sheet Layout and Types of Drawing
question: 1:10000 is enlarging scale.
explanation: 1:10000 is reducing scale since antecedent is less than consequent. The ratio represents the object should be drawn 1/10000th of the original one. Usually this much ratios will be used only when the machine parts are too big.
source: Engineering Drawing MCQs with explanations · p.8

subject: Engineering Drawing
topic: Sheet Layout and Types of Drawing (IS 962 layout of drawing)
subtopic: Sheet Layout and Types of Drawing
question: __________ is not an essential thing for free-hand sketching.
options: A paper in form of a sketch-book or a pad
explanation: French curves are used for drawing curves which cannot be drawn with a compass. Since we are just making a rough sketch of our drawing beforehand, for the actual drawing there is no need for French curves. The remaining are primary requirements to sketch any drawing.
source: Engineering Drawing MCQs with explanations · p.9

subject: Engineering Drawing
topic: Sheet Layout and Types of Drawing (IS 962 layout of drawing)
subtopic: Sheet Layout and Types of Drawing
question: Which statement is false?
options: Drawing for instruction manual: This is assembly drawing without dimensions. This is also used for explaining working principle of each part
Exploded assembly drawing: This type of assembly drawing is used for explaining working principle of any machine
Drawing for catalogue: Special assembly drawings are prepared for catalogues, with overall and principal dimensions
Patent drawing: It is generally assembly drawing either in pictorial form or principal view of orthographic projection of machine
explanation: The correct statements are schematic assembly drawing: This type of assembly drawing is used for explaining working principle of any machine. Exploded assembly drawing: It represents the details of a machine in a pictorial form as it is assembled. It helps the mechanics for dismantling machine for repairing purpose.
source: Engineering Drawing MCQs with explanations · p.9

subject: Engineering Drawing
topic: Sheet Layout and Types of Drawing (IS 962 layout of drawing)
subtopic: Sheet Layout and Types of Drawing
question: Arrange the statements. Given statements refers to free-hand sketching of straight lines. i) Then begin to draw the line with short and light strokes. ii) Hold the pencil at about 30 mm distance from the lead point. iii) Finish finally with a dark and firm line. iv) Swing it from left to right and backwards, between the two points.
explanation: Holding the pencil should be primary thing, getting clear view on drawing is next, after we have to just draw with a light sketch so that we can understand how the sketch will be, and finishing with a dark sketch.
source: Engineering Drawing MCQs with explanations · p.9

subject: Engineering Drawing
topic: Sheet Layout and Types of Drawing (IS 962 layout of drawing)
subtopic: Sheet Layout and Types of Drawing
question: Arrange the statements. Given statements refers to free-hand sketching of a circle. i) Add four radial lines between them. ii) Make the center and through it, draw horizontal and vertical center lines. iii) The paper may be revolved after about each quarter-circle for easy wrist motion while drawing. iv) Mark points on these lines at radius distance from the center.
explanation: For drawing, circle center should be the primary thing. Make the circle and through it draw horizontal and vertical center lines. Later we add four radial lines between them and then the paper maybe revolved for easy wrist motion to enable drawing. Different Types of Lines –
source: Engineering Drawing MCQs with explanations · p.10

subject: Engineering Drawing
question: Medium thickness, line-group of 2mm are not used for _________
explanation: Out lines, dotted lines and cutting plane-lines are drawn using 2mm thickness lines. Whereas centre lines, section lines, dimension lines, extension lines, construction lines, leader lines, short break lines and long-break lines are drawn using 1mm thickness lines.
source: Engineering Drawing MCQs with explanations · p.10

subject: Engineering Drawing
question: Initial work and construction lines are drawn using __ pencil.
explanation: Initial work and construction lines are drawn using H pencil. 2H pencil is used for outlines, dotted lines, dimension lines and arrowheads. 3H, 4H are used for centre lines and section lines.
source: Engineering Drawing MCQs with explanations · p.10

subject: Engineering Drawing
question: Centre lines, section lines are drawn using __ pencil.
explanation: Centre lines, section lines are drawn using 3H or 4H pencil. Outlines, dotted lines, section-plane lines, dimension lines and arrow heads are drawn using 2H. These different pencils give different shades which give different importance to lines in drawing.
source: Engineering Drawing MCQs with explanations · p.10

subject: Engineering Drawing
question: The line given below is used for____________
explanation: Lines used to represent cutting planes is chain thin (narrow) with thick (wide) at the ends and at changing of position, lines used to represent centroidal lines and outlines of adjacent parts are chain thin double-dashed or long-dashed double-dotted (narrow).
source: Engineering Drawing MCQs with explanations · p.11

subject: Engineering Drawing
question: The line given below is used for_________________
explanation: Hidden outlines, hidden edges are drawn using dashed thin (narrow) lines. Dimension lines are drawn using continuous thin (narrow) lines (straight or curved). The given type of line in question is used to represent cutting planes.
source: Engineering Drawing MCQs with explanations · p.11

subject: Engineering Drawing
question: Drawing pencils are graded according to increase in relative __________
explanation: Drawing pencils are graded according to increase in relative hardness. They are marketed with the labeled as H, 2H, 3H, 4H, 5H, 6H etc. These grades are used for getting accurate, clean and neat drawings.
source: Engineering Drawing MCQs with explanations · p.12

subject: Engineering Drawing
question: Outlines iv.Continuous thin lines
explanation: Dimension lines are continuous thin lines, are terminated at the outer ends by pointed arrowheads. Extension lines continuous thin lines extend by about 3mm beyond the dimension lines. Margin lines are continuous thick or wide lines along which the prints are trimmed. Outlines are continuous thick or wide lines.
source: Engineering Drawing MCQs with explanations · p.13

subject: Engineering Drawing
question: Short-break lines are drawn freehand while long-break lines are ruled lines.
explanation: Short-break lines are continuous, thin and wavy. They are drawn with freehand and are used to show a short-break, or irregular boundaries. Long-break lines are thin ruled lines with short zigzags within them. Different Types of Lines –
source: Engineering Drawing MCQs with explanations · p.13

subject: Engineering Drawing
question: In engineering drawing, which type of line indicates that there is a change of plane?
explanation: In engineering drawing, a change of plane is indicated by drawing continuous thick lines. Continuous thin lines are used for indicating dimension line, hatching line, revolved section, etc. Long chain lines are used to indicate center line, cutting lines.
source: Engineering Drawing MCQs with explanations · p.14

subject: Engineering Drawing
question: Which of the following lines are used to show that the object is cut and then viewed?
explanation: Hatching lines are used to show that the orthographic view is drawn after a section of the object is cut. They indicate that the object is cut and it shows the remaining solid body. Hidden lines are used to indicate holes or slots.
source: Engineering Drawing MCQs with explanations · p.14

subject: Engineering Drawing
question: What do hidden lines in orthographic projections denote?
options: Centre of a circle or cylinder
explanation: Hidden lines denote those parts which cannot be seen when viewing the object. They are used when there are holes or slots in the object, if they cannot be viewed directly. Change of plane is indicated by outlines. Position of cut is denoted by section line.
source: Engineering Drawing MCQs with explanations · p.14

subject: Engineering Drawing
question: What is the type of line used for line a?
explanation: Continuous thin straight lines are used to denote the dimensions of the object. Thin lines are used so as to distinguish between outline and the dimension line. Continuous thin wavy lines are used to indicate short breaks or irregular boundary line.
source: Engineering Drawing MCQs with explanations · p.15

subject: Engineering Drawing
question: The axis of the cylinder or sphere is denoted by which of the following line?
explanation: Centre line shows the axis of the cylinder or sphere. These lines generally pass through the centre of the circle. For a cylinder, they generally are parallel to the height of the cylinder. For circles, two centre lines are drawn perpendicular to each other passing through the centre of the circle.
source: Engineering Drawing MCQs with explanations · p.15

subject: Engineering Drawing
question: What is the standard length and width of the arrowhead of dimension lines?
explanation: Arrowheads of dimension lines have a length of 3mm and 1mm wide. When drawing the arrowheads the ratio, length: width is to be maintained at 3:1. The arrowheads can be drawn with length 6mm and breadth 2mm, since the ratio is the same.
source: Engineering Drawing MCQs with explanations · p.16

subject: Engineering Drawing
question: What is the length of the short dashes of the centre lines?
explanation: Centre line consists of long dash of 8-10mm, a gap of 1mm, short dash of 2mm and then a gap of 1mm. This pattern continues throughout the centre line. In case of section line, the ends of the section line are thickened. This is how section line and centre line are different.
source: Engineering Drawing MCQs with explanations · p.16

subject: Engineering Drawing
question: Which type of line is used to join the dimension line and the curve that needs to be dimensioned?
explanation: Leader lines lead the dimension line to the curve that needs to be dimensioned. It is a bridge connecting two lines. Outlines are the main or most prominent lines of the object when viewed for drawing. Dimension lines are used to denote the particular dimensions.
source: Engineering Drawing MCQs with explanations · p.16

subject: Engineering Drawing
question: What is the difference between the section line and the centre line?
options: The length of the long dashes
The two ends of the lines
explanation: The ends of a section line are thickened so as to distinguish it from the centre line. The rest of the section line has the same thickness and dimensions as that of the centre line. The thickening of the ends in the section line is also used to denote the direction of viewing.
source: Engineering Drawing MCQs with explanations · p.17

subject: Engineering Drawing
question: Which are the two systems of placing dimensions? (Options given below) i. Aligned system, ii. Break system, iii. Unidirectional system, iv. Directional system
explanation: The two systems of placing dimensions are aligned system and unidirectional system. In the aligned system the dimension is placed perpendicular to the dimension line. In unidirectional system all dimensions are placed such that they can be read from the bottom of the drawing sheet.
source: Engineering Drawing MCQs with explanations · p.17

subject: Engineering Drawing
question: Aligned system is used for drawing of air crafts, automobiles.
explanation: Since the drawing of aircrafts, automobiles etc. are very large it is inconvenient to read dimensions from the right-hand side. So we use unidirectional system of dimensioning but not aligned system of dimensioning.
source: Engineering Drawing MCQs with explanations · p.18

subject: Engineering Drawing
question: In unidirectional system the dimensions are ______
options: Placed by breaking the dimension line in the middle
Placed left side of the dimension line
explanation: In unidirectional system all dimensions are placed such that they can be read from the bottom of the drawing sheet. The dimension lines are broken near the middle for inserting the dimensions. This is used in mainly large drawings.
source: Engineering Drawing MCQs with explanations · p.18

subject: Engineering Drawing
question: In aligned system the dimensions are __________
options: Placed parallel to the dimension line
Placed perpendicular to the dimension line
Placed left side of the dimension line
Placed right side of the dimension line
explanation: In the aligned system the dimension is placed perpendicular to the dimension line. The dimensions should be placed near the middle and above, but clear of the dimension lines.
source: Engineering Drawing MCQs with explanations · p.18

subject: Engineering Drawing
question: In which system of dimensioning the figures can read from bottom as well as right hand side of the drawing?
explanation: In aligned system of dimensioning, the dimension figures are written in such a way that they can read from the bottom and right hand side of the drawing. It increases the effort in reading the dimensions. System of Dimensioning –
source: Engineering Drawing MCQs with explanations · p.19

subject: Engineering Drawing
question: Which of the following dimension is according to the ‘aligned system’ of dimensioning?
explanation: In aligned system of dimensioning, the dimensions are written on the dimension line. Their alignment is along the length of the dimension line. The dimensions are always written either on top or below the dimension line but never cutting it.
source: Engineering Drawing MCQs with explanations · p.20

subject: Engineering Drawing
question: In dimensioning, the lines enclosing the dimension line are known as ____
explanation: The extension line encloses the dimension line. It starts and ends with the line to be dimensioned. The extension line is extended beyond the dimension line by 4mm. It helps in defining proper boundaries for the dimension line.
source: Engineering Drawing MCQs with explanations · p.20

subject: Engineering Drawing
question: When dimensioning the circle, the dimension line begins from the centre of the circle.
explanation: When dimensioning the circle, the dimension line begins from the centre of the circle. With the help of the leader line, the dimensions are written on it. The notations φ and R are used to indicate whether the dimension denotes diameter or the radius respectively.
source: Engineering Drawing MCQs with explanations · p.21

subject: Engineering Drawing
question: While dimensioning a circle, the leader line and the dimension line are drawn at which angle with respect to each other?
explanation: When dimensioning a circle, the leader line and the dimension line are drawn 0˚ or 180˚ with respect to each other. This helps in clear dimensioning of the circle. It also reduces the difficulty in reading the dimensions when there are concentric circles involved.
source: Engineering Drawing MCQs with explanations · p.21

subject: Engineering Drawing
question: While dimensioning holes, slots, etc. how would their number be specified?
options: Number written on the dimension line
Number is written of the leader line
Number is written on the corner of the page
Number is written on the side of the hole or slot.
explanation: The number of holes, slots, etc. is written on the dimension line along with the dimensions. For example, if there are four holes of same dimensions; then only one of the holes will have their dimensions specified and along with dimensions, the number is also written; 4Holes, φx mm.
source: Engineering Drawing MCQs with explanations · p.21

subject: Engineering Drawing
question: What is the height if the dimension figures written on the dimension line?
explanation: It is customary to write the figures with a height of 3mm to 5mm. This helps in the readability of the dimension figures. It also makes reading the dimensions easy. The thickness of the letters is so adjusted that it can read without effort.
source: Engineering Drawing MCQs with explanations · p.21

subject: Engineering Drawing
question: In unidirectional system, the figures are written along the dimension line.
explanation: In unidirectional system of dimensioning, the dimension figures are written in between the dimension line. All dimensions are aligned according to the observer i.e. all are written in horizontal direction and not along the length of the dimension line.
source: Engineering Drawing MCQs with explanations · p.22

subject: Engineering Drawing
question: In which system of dimensioning the figures can read from bottom only?
explanation: In unidirectional system of dimensioning, the dimension figures are so written that they can be read only when viewed from the bottom and not from any other direction. Reading the dimensions is easier than in aligned system. Types of Dimensioning –
source: Engineering Drawing MCQs with explanations · p.22

subject: Engineering Drawing
question: The ratio of height to length of an arrow in dimensioning is ___
explanation: The standard ratio of height to length of an arrow in dimensioning should be kept only 1:3. Even if there are so many types of arrows like oblique stroke, closed, open small open circle etc. Generally closed and filled arrowhead is widely used and with 1:3 ratio.
source: Engineering Drawing MCQs with explanations · p.23

subject: Engineering Drawing
question: Dimensioning doesn’t represent _____
explanation: Dimensioning relates to the geometry of machine part/plot but not the material, transparency, physical, mechanical, chemical properties of machine part/plot. Other than the dimensions are placed near the title block of drawing sheet if necessary.
source: Engineering Drawing MCQs with explanations · p.23

subject: Engineering Drawing
question: Which is the wrong statement regarding dimensions?
options: Every dimension must be given, but none should be given more than once.
Every dimension should be written to the left side of the drawing.
Dimensions should be placed outside the views.
A centre line should not be used as dimension line.
explanation: There is no such rule that the dimensions should be placed only on left side of drawing because, it may not possible to represent every dimension only on left side. So, it is given flexibility that dimensions can be given any side of drawing but none should be given twice or more.
source: Engineering Drawing MCQs with explanations · p.23

subject: Engineering Drawing
question: Dimension lines should be drawn at least ________mm away from the outlines and from each other.
explanation: The standards are made as such that dimension lines should be drawn at least 8 mm away from the outlines and from each other. This gives clear, neat appearance in mentioning dimensions in drawing.
source: Engineering Drawing MCQs with explanations · p.23

subject: Engineering Drawing
question: Two types of dimensions needed on a drawing are: i) size or functional dimensions and ii) location or datum dimensions.
explanation: Yes, the given statement is true. The former indicate sizes i.e. length, breadth, height, depth, etc. The second one shows locations or exact positions of various constructional details within the object.
source: Engineering Drawing MCQs with explanations · p.24

subject: Engineering Drawing
question: An outline or a centre line should be used as a dimension line.
explanation: An outline or a centre line should never be used as a dimension line. A centre line may be extended to serve as an extension line. Since, the outline may be misunderstood if it is used as dimension line.
source: Engineering Drawing MCQs with explanations · p.24

subject: Engineering Drawing
question: Which is the wrong statement from the below options?
options: As far as possible all dimensions should be given in millimeters, omitting the abbreviation mm.
The height of the dimension figures should be from 3mm to 5mm.
A zero must always precede the decimal point when the dimension is less than unity
The dimensions should only be given in mm
explanation: There is no need to give the dimensions only in mm. Some of the drawings may be very large in size it is not convenient to give dimensions in millimeters and another unit is used but only one dimension should be used among whole drawing.
source: Engineering Drawing MCQs with explanations · p.25

subject: Engineering Drawing
question: Location and datum dimensions indicates __________
explanation: The location or datum dimension which are generally shown by letters F and L respectively, and shows the location or exact position of various constructional details within the object. The letter F represents functional dimensions.
source: Engineering Drawing MCQs with explanations · p.25

subject: Engineering Drawing
question: Size or functional dimensions does not indicate _________________
explanation: Size or functional dimensions only represents dimensions, figures of length, breadth, height, depth, and diameter. But not show the locations or positions these are indicated by location or datum dimensions. Types of Dimensioning –
source: Engineering Drawing MCQs with explanations · p.25

subject: Engineering Drawing
question: In chain dimension, the dimensions are arranged parallel to each other.
explanation: In chain dimension, the dimensions are arranged in a straight line. The type of dimensioning in which the dimensions are arranged parallel to each other is called as Parallel Dimension. The combination of both the type is called as combined dimension.
source: Engineering Drawing MCQs with explanations · p.26

subject: Engineering Drawing
question: In combined dimension, the dimensions are arranged in a straight line only.
explanation: In combined type of dimension, the dimensions are arranged in a straight line as well as parallel to each other. It depends on the convenience of dimensioning and the important dimensions. When more than two dimensions overlap, combined dimensioning is done.
source: Engineering Drawing MCQs with explanations · p.26

subject: Engineering Drawing
question: In which of the following type of dimensioning, the dimensions are arranged only in a straight line?
explanation: In chain dimension, the dimensions are arranged only in a straight line. In this type of dimensioning, the dimensions appear less crowded and make it easier to read. There is almost less confusion while interpreting the dimensions.
source: Engineering Drawing MCQs with explanations · p.26

subject: Engineering Drawing
question: Which type of dimensioning is done below?
explanation: The dimension figures are written in such a way that they can be read from bottom only. The chain dimensioning is used as the dimensions are arranged in a straight line. In parallel dimension, the dimension lines are arranged parallel to each other.
source: Engineering Drawing MCQs with explanations · p.27

subject: Engineering Drawing
question: Identify the type of dimensioning used in the example below.
explanation: The type of dimensioning done is combined dimensioning and the system of dimensioning used is aligned. The dimensions are arranged in both ways i.e. parallel as well as in a straight line. The dimension figures are aligned along the length of the dimension line.
source: Engineering Drawing MCQs with explanations · p.29

subject: Engineering Drawing
question: Which type of dimensioning is done in the example below?
explanation: The dimensions are arranged parallel to each other in horizontal dimensioning and in straight line for vertical dimensioning. There is a need for calculation for finding out some dimensions. The dimension figures can be read only from the bottom.
source: Engineering Drawing MCQs with explanations · p.30

subject: Engineering Drawing
question: Identify the type and system of dimensioning in the example given below.
explanation: The example has unidirectional and chain type of dimensioning. The dimension figures are arranged horizontally and can only be read from the bottom. The dimensions are arranged in a straight line and not in parallel direction. Basic Principles in Dimensioning -1
source: Engineering Drawing MCQs with explanations · p.30

subject: Engineering Drawing
question: The advised position of placement of the dimensions should be ______
options: On the boundaries of the view
explanation: It is advised to place the dimensions outside the view. This will bring clear picture of the view and will help in the understanding of the dimensions. Placing the dimensions outside the view gives a cleaner look.
source: Engineering Drawing MCQs with explanations · p.31

subject: Engineering Drawing
question: Which of the following dimensions is arranged haphazardly?
explanation: The dimension 30mm is repeated and is placed in a haphazard manner. There is no need for the dimension in F.V. as it is clearly understood from the S.V. Such dimensions should be avoided at all costs.
source: Engineering Drawing MCQs with explanations · p.32

subject: Engineering Drawing
question: If there is a need for the center line, then it can be used as a _____
explanation: The center line can be used an extension line. With the help of the center line as extension line, we can dimension the distance between the centers of the circles from the outline view of the object. Thus helps in drawing the circle accurately.
source: Engineering Drawing MCQs with explanations · p.32

subject: Engineering Drawing
question: Which of the following dimension is incorrect?
explanation: The dimension 20mm is given without using the extension line. The outline of the view is used to dimension the line. This is not usually favoured. Always use extension line and place the dimension line in between the extension lines.
source: Engineering Drawing MCQs with explanations · p.33

subject: Engineering Drawing
question: Dimension lines should not intersect each other as far as possible.
explanation: Dimension should never intersect each other as far possible. Intersecting dimension lines can cause confusion and needs more effort to understand them. To increase the readability of the dimension they should not intersect with each other.
source: Engineering Drawing MCQs with explanations · p.33

subject: Engineering Drawing
question: Different units of measurement can be used in dimensioning a view.
explanation: All dimensions should be expressed in one unit. Using different units for dimensions will create confusion for the observer and there is a chance of misinterpretation. Therefore, using different units should be avoided and a tag ‘All dimensions are in mm’ should be added above the title page.
source: Engineering Drawing MCQs with explanations · p.34

subject: Engineering Drawing
question: While dimensioning a cylinder in the view where the true shape of the cylinder is not visible, which symbol is used to denote that it is a cylinder?
explanation: Since the true shape of the cylinder is circle from one view, we used the symbol φ followed by the dimension figure while dimensioning it in the view where it is seen as a rectangle. The cross-section of the rectangle is square then the symbol • followed by the dimension figure is used.
source: Engineering Drawing MCQs with explanations · p.34

subject: Engineering Drawing
question: As far as possible, dimension should be given to which of the following lines?
explanation: Dimensions are given to the outlines of the view. It is advised not to dimension hidden lines as their true shape is not known when they hidden. It is important to dimension those lines whose true shape is properly visible.
source: Engineering Drawing MCQs with explanations · p.34

subject: Engineering Drawing
question: How is a spot face hole with 24mm diameter, 5mm deep and spot face diameter 10mm dimensioned?
options: φ10 SPOT FACE, φ24 x 5 DEEP
explanation: Holes made by spot facing are dimensioned in this manner ‘φ10 SPOT FACE, φ24 x 5 DEEP’. This means the there is a spot face of 10mm diameter after the 24mm diameter and 5 mm thickness. Using this makes the reading of the dimension easy. Basic Principles in Dimensioning –
source: Engineering Drawing MCQs with explanations · p.34

subject: Engineering Drawing
question: How is tapped hole of diameter 10mm with 20mm dimensioned?
explanation: A tapped hole of 10mm diameter and 20mm deep is dimensioned as M10, DEEP 20. The ‘M’ stands for metric threads. These are standard threads whose pitch is predefined according to the diameter. The ‘M’ indicates that the hole is tapped.
source: Engineering Drawing MCQs with explanations · p.35

subject: Engineering Drawing
question: How is a blind drilled hole of 15mm diameter and 15mm deep dimensioned?
explanation: Since the hole is not through, it is mandatory to mention the depth of the hole while dimensioning. Hence a blind drilled hole of 15mm diameter and 15mm deep is dimensioned as φ15, DEEP 15. Since the hole is not threaded ‘M’ should not be used for dimensioning.
source: Engineering Drawing MCQs with explanations · p.35

subject: Engineering Drawing
question: The dimensions of circular part or arc should be given where the true shape is visible.
explanation: Circular parts and arcs should be dimensioned where their true shapes are visible. Proper notations should be used to dimension circles and arcs. This will help in clarifying the dimension and reduces the confusion if there are any.
source: Engineering Drawing MCQs with explanations · p.35

subject: Engineering Drawing
question: A chamfer of 3mm thick and angle 45˚ inclination is dimensioned as _____
explanation: A chamfer of 3mm thickness and angle 45˚ is dimensioned as 3 x 45˚. From this dimension, we can get the information of the angle at which the chamfer is cut and the distance from one of the sides. This helps in reading of the dimensions easy.
source: Engineering Drawing MCQs with explanations · p.36

subject: Engineering Drawing
question: The leader should be used to dimension the circle.
explanation: The leader lines should be used to dimension the circle. This helps in identifying the true shape as well the dimension related to the circle. It is advised not to dimension cylinders in the views where it is seen as any shape other than circle but should be dimensioned where its cross-section is clearly visible.
source: Engineering Drawing MCQs with explanations · p.36

subject: Engineering Drawing
question: What does dimensioning of a circle depend upon?
explanation: The dimensioning of the circle depends upon the size or diameter of the circle. If the diameter of the circle is considerably large, the dimension can be given inside the circle itself. It should be noted that the dimension of the circle should be given in the view where its true shape is visible.
source: Engineering Drawing MCQs with explanations · p.36

subject: Engineering Drawing
question: The dimensions which are smaller are to be placed _______
options: Further from the outline of the view
explanation: The dimensions which are smaller should be placed nearer to the view while the larger view should be place further away. Dimensions large or small should not be placed on the view. Extension lines should be used and the outlines of ht view for dimensioning.
source: Engineering Drawing MCQs with explanations · p.36

subject: Engineering Drawing
question: While dimensioning, where should the large dimensions be placed?
options: On the outlines of the view
explanation: The larger dimensions should be placed further away from the outlines of the view. They should be placed beyond the smaller dimensions. This helps in a neat arrangement of the dimensions and can be understood easily.
source: Engineering Drawing MCQs with explanations · p.37

subject: Engineering Drawing
question: Extension lines should start from which part of the drawing?
explanation: Extension lines should start immediately from the outlines of the views. There should be no gap between the outlines and the extension lines. Dimensions should not be given on the outlines themselves and therefore extension lines should be used.
source: Engineering Drawing MCQs with explanations · p.37

subject: Engineering Drawing
question: Dimensions can be placed anywhere irrespective of the features visible.
explanation: Dimensions have to be placed where the true shape or features are clearly indicated. For example, if there is cylindrical hole in the object, the size of the cylinder i.e. the diameter of the base circle should be dimensioned in the view where it is seen as circle and not in the view where the cylinder is seen as rectangle. Terminology of Dimensioning –
source: Engineering Drawing MCQs with explanations · p.37

subject: Engineering Drawing
question: Identify the ‘a’ in the given picture
explanation: Centre line usually represents the centre of circle, the axis of cylindrical objects, lines of symmetry, trajectories, pitch circle of gears and pitch circle of holes, represented by chain thin long-dashed dotted (narrow).
source: Engineering Drawing MCQs with explanations · p.38

subject: Engineering Drawing
question: Identify the ‘a’ in the below given picture.
explanation: An extension line also a thin continuous line drawn in extension of an outline. It extends by about 3 mm beyond the dimension line. Dimension line is a thin continuous line. It is terminated by arrowheads touching the outlines, extension lines or centre lines.
source: Engineering Drawing MCQs with explanations · p.38

subject: Engineering Drawing
question: While representing the diameter in dimensioning it is represented as __________
explanation: Diameter is represented the unique way as shown in options which directly represents the circle and line at its center that is center line where diameter is measured. But radius is represented as capital R.
source: Engineering Drawing MCQs with explanations · p.39

subject: Engineering Drawing
question: It is recommended that a gap of about 2 mm should be kept between the extension line and an outline.
explanation: It is recommended that a gap of about 1 mm should be kept between the extension line and an outline or object boundary by the B.I.S. It extends by about 3 mm beyond the dimension line.
source: Engineering Drawing MCQs with explanations · p.41

subject: Engineering Drawing
question: A dot may also be used to replace an arrowhead.
explanation: Arrowheads should ordinarily be drawn within the dimensioned feature. But when there is fewer space arrowheads can also be kept outside and a dot may also be used to replace arrowhead and also if there is no space for dimension figure to be kept on dimension line the figure may be written above the extended portion of dimension line. Terminology of Dimensioning –
source: Engineering Drawing MCQs with explanations · p.41

subject: Engineering Drawing
question: Which of the lines is a thin continuous line with the ends terminating in arrowheads and is enclosed by extension lines, outlines or centre lines?
explanation: The dimension line is a thin continuous line with the ends terminating in arrowheads and is enclosed by extension lines, outlines or centre lines. The dimension figures is written on the top of the dimension line or aligned at the centre of the dimension line according to the system of dimensioning.
source: Engineering Drawing MCQs with explanations · p.41

subject: Engineering Drawing
question: What is the name of the thin continuous line which encloses the dimension lines are generally drawn 1mm away from the outlines?
explanation: Extension line is a thin continuous line which encloses the dimension line and they are generally drawn 1mm away from the outlines. They need to drawn near to the outlines and far away from the outlines.
source: Engineering Drawing MCQs with explanations · p.41

subject: Engineering Drawing
question: In engineering drawing, which type of arrowhead is used?
explanation: Usually in engineering drawing, the arrowheads used are closed and neatly filled. They are made by hand in proportion to the thickness of the outline. The length of the arrowhead is three times the width of the arrowhead.
source: Engineering Drawing MCQs with explanations · p.42

subject: Engineering Drawing
question: What is used to specify the operation done on a particular feature?
explanation: A note is used to indicate information about the operation done on a particular feature. It is written near to the feature and usually it is shown outside the view. With this type of information of the drawing manufacturing of the part becomes easy.
source: Engineering Drawing MCQs with explanations · p.42

subject: Engineering Drawing
question: Which of the following is a thin continuous line with one side terminating in arrowhead and the other with a period?
explanation: A leader is thin continuous line with one end terminating in arrowhead and the other with a period. While dimensioning arcs or circles, leaders are aligned to the radius of the respective arcs or circles.
source: Engineering Drawing MCQs with explanations · p.42

subject: Engineering Drawing
question: What is the inclination of the leader in a drawing?
explanation: The leaders are drawn at an inclination of more than 30˚. They should not be placed vertical, horizontal and less than 30˚ to the respective feature. The arrowhead should touch the feature they are describing or dimensioning.
source: Engineering Drawing MCQs with explanations · p.43

subject: Engineering Drawing
question: A leader line can be drawn curved.
explanation: A leader line can never be drawn curved. They should be drawn straight and inclined at an angle not less than 30˚. They should not be placed vertical or horizontal in the views. One side of the leader line should terminate in arrowhead and the other in period.
source: Engineering Drawing MCQs with explanations · p.43

subject: Engineering Drawing
question: Which of the following dimension needs to be calculated?
explanation: In the given example, the diameter of the circle is not dimensioned. Diameter of a circle is a very prominent feature and should not be missed while dimensioning. The dimensions are so given that they do not require any further calculations. The above example is the incorrect way of dimensioning.
source: Engineering Drawing MCQs with explanations · p.43

subject: Engineering Drawing
question: Operations performed on a particular feature are indicated by using extension lines.
explanation: A note is used to indicate the operations done on a feature if there any. The note accompanied by a leader line which terminates in arrowhead on one side and a period on other side. For example, the threads on feature may have a note indicating whether it is a single start or double start.
source: Engineering Drawing MCQs with explanations · p.44

subject: Engineering Drawing
question: Tapers and slope indicated in the view are part of dimensioning.
explanation: Tapers and slopes are part of dimensioning. They are calculated through their respective formulas and are indicated as 1: x, near the feature which has the slope or taper on them. While drawing these features, having this information sure comes handy. Representative Factor –
source: Engineering Drawing MCQs with explanations · p.44

subject: Engineering Drawing
question: Representative fraction is the ____________________
options: ratio of the length in drawing to the actual length
ratio of the actual length to the length in drawing
square of the length in drawing
explanation: Representative fraction is the ratio of the length of the object represented on drawing to the actual length of the object represented.
source: Engineering Drawing MCQs with explanations · p.45

subject: Engineering Drawing
question: The scale of a drawing is given as 1:20. What is the representative fraction?
explanation: The scale of drawing is given as 1:20 that is a reducing scale, this means dimensions are made to 1/20th of full size. So the representative factor is that dimension in drawing to actual dimension. R.F. = (1/20)/1 = 1/20.
source: Engineering Drawing MCQs with explanations · p.45

subject: Engineering Drawing
question: The scale of a drawing is given as 15:1. What is the representative fraction?
explanation: The scale of drawing is given as 15:1 that is a enlarging scale, this means dimensions are increased to 15 times of actual ones. So the representative factor is that dimension in drawing to actual dimension. R.F. = 15/1 = 15.
source: Engineering Drawing MCQs with explanations · p.45

subject: Engineering Drawing
question: The length of the drawing is 50 mm, the scale is given as 1:5. Find the actual length.
explanation: The scale given is 1:5 (reducing scale) that is the drawing is made with 1/5th of actual dimensions. So we have to multiply the drawing length with 5. 50 mm x 5 =250 mm and 1 cm =10 mm. The actual length in cm is 25.
source: Engineering Drawing MCQs with explanations · p.45

subject: Engineering Drawing
question: The actual length is 1m. The length of drawing is 5cm. Find the representative factor.
explanation: Representative factor is the ratio of the length represented in drawing to the actual length. Here given actual length is 1 m =100cm and length of drawing is 5 cm. R.F. =5 cm/100 cm = 0.05 (or) = 1/20.
source: Engineering Drawing MCQs with explanations · p.46

subject: Engineering Drawing
question: The representative factor is 4. The actual length is 20 mm. Find the length of drawing.
explanation: The representative factor given is 4 (more than one), shows the scale is enlarging. Representative factor = ratio of length in drawing to actual length. R.F. = (length in drawing)/20 mm = 4. Length in drawing = 20 mm x 4 = 80 mm = 8 cm.
source: Engineering Drawing MCQs with explanations · p.46

subject: Engineering Drawing
question: A machine part is drawn two times with different scales. The ratio of 1st drawing’s R.F. to 2nd drawing R.F. with respect to actual object is found to be 2. The length of second drawing is 10 mm. Find the 1st drawing length.
explanation: 2= 1st drawing R.F/2nd drawing R.F. =(length of 1st drawing/ actual length)/(length of 2nd drawing/ actual length) = length of first drawing/ length of second drawing= length of first drawing/ 10 mm. 2 x 10 mm = 20 mm. So therefore the length of first drawing is 20 mm = 2 cm.
source: Engineering Drawing MCQs with explanations · p.46

subject: Engineering Drawing
question: The length of the drawing is 20 cm, the scale is given as 2:1. Find the actual length.
explanation: The scale given is 2:1 (enlarging scale) that is the drawing is made 2 times of actual dimensions. So we have to divide the drawing length with 2. 20 mm / 2 =100 mm and 1 cm =10 mm. The actual length in cm is 10 cm.
source: Engineering Drawing MCQs with explanations · p.47

subject: Engineering Drawing
question: The actual length is 1cm. The length of drawing is 30 cm. Find the representative factor.
explanation: Representative factor is the ratio of the length represented in drawing to the actual length. Here given actual length is 1 cm and length of drawing is 30 cm. R.F. =30 cm/1 cm = 30.
source: Engineering Drawing MCQs with explanations · p.47

subject: Engineering Drawing
question: The representative factor is 0.02. The actual length is 50 cm. Find the length of drawing.
explanation: The representative factor given is 0.02 (less than one), shows the reducing scale. Representative factor = ratio of length in drawing to actual length. R.F. = (length in drawing)/50 cm = 0.02. Length in drawing = 0.02 x 50 cm = 1 cm = 10 mm.
source: Engineering Drawing MCQs with explanations · p.47

subject: Engineering Drawing
question: The ratio of length of actual object to length of drawing is given as 5. Find the scale and R.F. (Representative factor).
explanation: Given that the ratio of actual length to length of drawing which is reciprocal of R.F. So the R.F. for given values is 1/5. From the given information it can be understood that the actual object is 5 times larger than the drawing, so the scale is reducing scale i.e. 1:5.
source: Engineering Drawing MCQs with explanations · p.47

subject: Engineering Drawing
question: The representative factor is 2, the drawing length is 100 mm. Find the actual length.
explanation: The scale is enlarging scale. The ratio of length of drawing to actual length gives the representative factor. 100 mm / actual length = 2, actual length = 100 mm/2 = actual length = 50 mm (or) 5 cm.
source: Engineering Drawing MCQs with explanations · p.48

subject: Engineering Drawing
question: The representative factor is 0.5, the drawing length is 10 cm. Find the actual length.
explanation: The scale is reducing scale. The ratio of length of drawing to actual length gives the representative factor. 10 cm / actual length = 0.5, actual length = 10 cm/0.5 = actual length = 20 cm (or) 200 mm. Representative Factor –
source: Engineering Drawing MCQs with explanations · p.48

subject: Engineering Drawing
question: Representative factor is defined as the ratio of the length of the drawing to the actual length of the object.
explanation: The representative factor is defined as the ratio of the length of the drawing to the actual length of the object. The value of representative factor can give information on whether the scale is enlarging or reducing.
source: Engineering Drawing MCQs with explanations · p.48

subject: Engineering Drawing
question: What is the representative factor of a line, whose length is 24cm on the drawing sheet, representing an actual length of 6m?
explanation: Representative factor is calculated as the ratio of the length of the drawing to the actual length of the object. Both the quantities should be taken in same unit. In this example, R.F. equals to 24 ÷ (600) i.e. 1:25.
source: Engineering Drawing MCQs with explanations · p.49

subject: Engineering Drawing
question: A 20mm line, drawn on the drawing sheet represents an actual length of 5m. What is the representative factor?
explanation: The formula for calculating the representative factor is the length of the drawing divided by the actual length of the object. Hence for this example, R.F = 20 ÷ 5000 i.e. 1:250. The units of the quantities in the formula must be the same.
source: Engineering Drawing MCQs with explanations · p.49

subject: Engineering Drawing
question: A line of 10cm is drawn on a drawing sheet. It represents an actual length of 25mm. What is the representative factor?
explanation: Representative factor is calculated as the ratio of the length of the drawing to the actual length of the drawing it represents. From this formula we get, R.F. = 100 ÷ 25. Hence the representative factor is 4:1.
source: Engineering Drawing MCQs with explanations · p.49

subject: Engineering Drawing
question: Which of the following representative factor will have an enlarging scale?
explanation: The representative factor 1:0.5 can be written as 2:1. Since the actual length of the drawing is less than the representative length, the scale is enlarging. If the actual length of the object is greater than the representative value, R.F. will be less than unity.
source: Engineering Drawing MCQs with explanations · p.50

subject: Engineering Drawing
question: Which of the following representative factors depict that the actual length of the object is greater than the length of the drawing?
explanation: Considering that a 2cm line drawn on the drawing sheet represents an actual length of 5cm. Hence in the case of representative factor 2:5 i.e. 1:2.5, the actual length is greater than the length of the drawing.
source: Engineering Drawing MCQs with explanations · p.50

subject: Engineering Drawing
question: What is the representative factor if the length of the drawing is 15mm and the actual length of the object is 3m?
explanation: The representative factor is the ratio of length of the drawing to the actual length of an object. Hence for the line of length 15mm and the actual length 3m, R.F. = 15 ÷ 3000 = 1:200. The units of both the quantities should be same.
source: Engineering Drawing MCQs with explanations · p.50

subject: Engineering Drawing
question: Which of the following is not a valid representative factor?
explanation: The representative factor cannot be zero. As the length of the drawing cannot be zero, having a value zero means that there is no drawing made. Representative factors are used to scale down or up the drawing from the actual object.
source: Engineering Drawing MCQs with explanations · p.50

subject: Engineering Drawing
question: A line of length 4mm is represented by a line of 4cm. What is the representative factor?
explanation: The actual length of the object is 4mm and the length of the drawing is 4cm. From the formula for calculating the representative factor we get, R.F. = 4 ÷ 0.4 = 10. Hence the representative factor is 10:1.
source: Engineering Drawing MCQs with explanations · p.51

subject: Engineering Drawing
question: What is the representative factor if sides of square measuring 4cm in the drawing sheet while the actual length of the side of the square is 3m?
explanation: The length of the drawing is 4cm and the actual length of the drawing is 3m. By using the formula for calculating the representative factor we get the value of R.F. as 1:75. R.F. = 4 ÷ 300. The units of both the quantities should be the same. Types of Scales –
source: Engineering Drawing MCQs with explanations · p.51

subject: Engineering Drawing
question: What is the type of scale in which the representative fraction is 1:1?
explanation: A full size scale is a type of scale in which the length of the drawing and the actual length of the object is of the ratio 1:1. Hence by definition, its representative fraction is 1:1. In full size scale the drawing is drawn with the actual measurements.
source: Engineering Drawing MCQs with explanations · p.51

subject: Engineering Drawing
question: Which of the following representative fraction depicts an enlarging scale?
explanation: Enlarging scale means that the drawing is drawn with the bigger dimensions in comparison to the actual dimensions of the object. A representative fraction of 1:0.2 means 5:1, i.e. the drawing is five times bigger than the actual object. Hence the scale is enlarging scale.
source: Engineering Drawing MCQs with explanations · p.52

subject: Engineering Drawing
question: Which of the following scales is a reducing scale?
explanation: The representative fraction 1:3 indicates that the dimension of the drawing is one-third of the actual object. Since the drawing is smaller than the actual object, this type of scale is called reducing scale.
source: Engineering Drawing MCQs with explanations · p.52

subject: Engineering Drawing
question: Which of the following is not an enlarging scale?
explanation: Enlarging scale means that the drawing is larger than the actual object. Hence the representative fraction will be greater than unity. For reducing scale the representative fraction is less than unity.
source: Engineering Drawing MCQs with explanations · p.52

subject: Engineering Drawing
question: Which of the following scales is neither an enlarging nor a reducing scale?
explanation: A scale which is neither enlarging nor reducing is called as full size scale. The representative fraction of a full size scale is 1:1. In full size scale, the drawing is made just as the actual dimensions of the object.
source: Engineering Drawing MCQs with explanations · p.52

subject: Engineering Drawing
question: A scale which is numerically represented on the drawing sheet is called as _____
explanation: An engineer’s scale is the representation of the scale used in drawing on the drawing sheet numerically. For example, if the length of the drawing is 5 cm and the actual length is 10m, then it is numerically represented as 5cm = 10m.
source: Engineering Drawing MCQs with explanations · p.53

subject: Engineering Drawing
question: Which of the following scale is used in survey maps?
explanation: Graphical scales are used in survey maps. The graphical scale is drawn on the drawing. When the drawing ages, the engineer’s scale shrinks and may not give accurate results. Hence graphical scale is used as the drawing shrinks, the scale will also shrink.
source: Engineering Drawing MCQs with explanations · p.53

subject: Engineering Drawing
question: What is the formula for calculating the length of the scale?
options: Minimum length to be measured x R.F.
Minimum length to be measured ÷ R.F.
Maximum length to be measured ÷ R.F.
Maximum length to be measured x R.F.
explanation: The length of the scale is calculated by using the following formula, Length of the scale = R.F. x Maximum length to be measured.
source: Engineering Drawing MCQs with explanations · p.53

subject: Engineering Drawing
question: The minimum length to be shown must be known for drawing unusual scale.
explanation: The maximum length of the scale must be known to draw unusual scales on the drawing sheet. The representative fraction of the scale is also essential information. The units of the scale must be mentioned on the drawing. Types of Scales –
source: Engineering Drawing MCQs with explanations · p.54

subject: Engineering Drawing
question: What are the two parts of Vernier scale?
explanation: The Vernier scale consists of two parts. They are the primary scale and the Vernier scale. Vernier scale is used to read very small dimensions with great accuracy. The Vernier part of the scale is derived from the primary scale.
source: Engineering Drawing MCQs with explanations · p.54

subject: Engineering Drawing
question: Which of the following scale is a plain scale with fully divided minor divisions?
explanation: The primary scale is a plain scale with fully divided minor divisions. For reading very small dimensions, minor divisions cannot be further divided. Hence we use Vernier scale to read those dimensions.
source: Engineering Drawing MCQs with explanations · p.54

subject: Engineering Drawing
question: The graduations of which scale is derived from the primary scale?
explanation: The graduations on the primary scale helps in making the graduations on the Vernier scale. For reading very small dimensions we need to further divide the minor divisions on the primary scale, which will to problems in reading dimensions properly. Hence Vernier scale is used.
source: Engineering Drawing MCQs with explanations · p.54

subject: Engineering Drawing
question: Which of the following is used in checking the instruments to measure angles with great accuracy?
explanation: The circular Vernier scale is used to check the instruments to measure angles with high accuracy. They are used in measuring instruments like micrometer in mechanical engineering. They work on the same principle as the linear Vernier scale.
source: Engineering Drawing MCQs with explanations · p.55

subject: Engineering Drawing
question: Which of the following scales represent two different units having same representative fration?
explanation: Comparative scales are those in which two different units are measured by using different graduations but have same representative fraction. A drawing can be read in two units with the help of this scale.
source: Engineering Drawing MCQs with explanations · p.55

subject: Engineering Drawing
question: What is the length of the scale, the representative fraction is 1:50000 and the scale must measure up to 25 km?
explanation: The formula for calculating the length of the scale is given by, Length of the scale = R.F. x maximum length to be measured; Hence length of the scale = 1 ÷ 50000 x 25 x 1000 x 100 = 50 cm. It is very important to note the units while calculating.
source: Engineering Drawing MCQs with explanations · p.55

subject: Engineering Drawing
question: In a particular drawing, 40 inches is represented by a 10 cm long line. A comparative scale is constructed that measures up to 180 inches and 2 m respectively. What are the lengths of scale for both the inches as well as the meter scales? (1 inch = 0.0254 meter)
explanation: The length of the scale = R.F. x maximum length to be measured. Hence for the inches scale, R.F. = 10 ÷ 40 and the maximum length to be measured is 180 inches. Hence length of inch scale = 10 ÷ 40 x 180 = 45 cm. Similarly length of meter scale = 10 ÷ 40 ÷ 0.0254 ÷ 100 x 2 x 100 = 19.7 cm.
source: Engineering Drawing MCQs with explanations · p.56

subject: Engineering Drawing
question: Which of the following is used to set or measure angles when a protractor is not available?
explanation: The scale of chords is used to measure or set angles when there is no protractor. In this method, a line PQ is drawn and then from Q a perpendicular QR is drawn. An arc is drawn with centre Q and is made to intersect perpendicular QR. Then the arc is divided into 9 equal parts with each part denoting 10˚ from Q.
source: Engineering Drawing MCQs with explanations · p.56

subject: Engineering Drawing
question: In a map, 30 miles is represented by 20 cm. What is the length of the kilometer scale if the maximum length to be measured is 10 km? (1 mile = 1.609 km)
explanation: The formula for calculating the length of the scale is given by; Length of the scale = R.F. x maximum length to be measured. Hence from the formula, length of the scale = 20 ÷ (30 x 1.609 x 1000 x 100) x 10 x 1000 x 100 = 4.14 cm.
source: Engineering Drawing MCQs with explanations · p.56

subject: Engineering Drawing
question: What is the representative fraction of the kilometer scale if 20 miles is represented as 5 cm and maximum length to be measured is 5 km? (1 mile = 1.609 km)
explanation: The representative fraction is calculated by the formula, R.F. = length of the drawing ÷ actual length of the object. Here the length of the drawing is 5 cm and the actual length is 20 miles. In R.F. both quantities should be in same unit. R.F. = 5 ÷ (20 x 1.609 x1000 x 100) = 1:643600. Types of Scales –
source: Engineering Drawing MCQs with explanations · p.57

subject: Engineering Drawing
question: Why it is more beneficial to represent the scale graphically other than by just numerical?
explanation: The scale is drawn on the drawing itself. As the drawing becomes old, the drawing sheet may shrink and may not give accurate results then. But if we use graphical scale, along with drawing the scale also shrinks.
source: Engineering Drawing MCQs with explanations · p.57

subject: Engineering Drawing
question: What is not essential information to construct a scale from the following?
explanation: The length of the scale can be found using ’length of the scale = Representative fraction x Maximum length’. To draw drawing R.F (representative fraction), Units to represent (example: meters and centimeter or another if needed) and maximum length required is essential.
source: Engineering Drawing MCQs with explanations · p.57

subject: Engineering Drawing
question: Scales having same representative fraction but graduated to read different units are called ______________________
explanation: A drawing drawn with a scale reading inch units can be read in metric units by means of a metric comparative scale, constructed with same representative fraction. The comparative scales may be plain scales or diagonal scales and may be constructed separately or one above the other.
source: Engineering Drawing MCQs with explanations · p.58

subject: Engineering Drawing
question: The scale used in micrometer is _____________
explanation: The circular vernier uses the principle of vernier. The circular vernier is used in surveying instruments to measure angle to the required accuracy. In the case of mechanical engineering, it is used in measuring instruments like micrometer.
source: Engineering Drawing MCQs with explanations · p.58

subject: Engineering Drawing
question: The scale used to find angles is ________
explanation: The scale of chords is used to set out or measure angles when a protractor is not available. It is based on lengths of chords of different angles measured on the same arc.
source: Engineering Drawing MCQs with explanations · p.58

subject: Engineering Drawing
question: Which scale you prefer if there is need to measure most accurately.
explanation: The plain scale gives only up to single decimal. Comparative scales are just used to represent two different units. The vernier scale gives up to 2 decimal values.
source: Engineering Drawing MCQs with explanations · p.58

subject: Engineering Drawing
question: Which scale represents only two units or a unit and its sub-division?
explanation: A plain scale is constructed by dividing a line into suitable number of equal parts or units, the first of which is sub-divided into smaller parts. Plain scales represent either two units or a unit and its sub-division.
source: Engineering Drawing MCQs with explanations · p.59

subject: Engineering Drawing
question: Which scale is employed when we need to measure in three units?
explanation: A diagonal scale is used when very small distances are to be accurately measured or when measurements are required in three units. Small divisions of short lines are obtained by the principle of diagonal scales.
source: Engineering Drawing MCQs with explanations · p.59

subject: Engineering Drawing
question: We need a scale which has to show dm, cm and mm. Which scale do you prefer?
explanation: Diagonal scale is meant for drawing scales which represents 3 units. A diagonal scale is used when very minute distances to be measured. Small divisions of short lines are obtained by the principle of diagonal scale.
source: Engineering Drawing MCQs with explanations · p.59

subject: Engineering Drawing
question: Which scale is used in surveying instrument?
explanation: The circular vernier uses the principle of vernier. The circular vernier is used in surveying instruments to measure angle to the required accuracy. In the case of mechanical engineering, it is used in measuring instruments like micrometer. Plane Scales –
source: Engineering Drawing MCQs with explanations · p.60

subject: Engineering Drawing
question: The maximum length is 50 m and length of scale is 10 cm. Find the Representative factor.
explanation: Length of the scale = Representative fraction x Maximum length, 10 cm = Representative fraction x 5000 cm, Representative factor = 1/500.
source: Engineering Drawing MCQs with explanations · p.60

subject: Engineering Drawing
question: Given Representative factor as 4/50 and maximum length is 100 cm. Find the length of scale.
explanation: Length of the scale = Representative fraction x Maximum length, Length of scale = 4/50 x 100 cm, Length of scale= 8 cm.
source: Engineering Drawing MCQs with explanations · p.60

subject: Engineering Drawing
question: Given, below are the steps related to construct a scale of 1:50 to show meters and decimeters and maximum length is 5 meters. Arrange the steps i. Draw a line 10 cm long and divide it to 5 equal parts
explanation: The general procedure involves finding R.F. at the 1st and next max length of scale and then dividing whole line into given number of units at last dividing the 1st part to number of sub-divisions that occur in unit.
source: Engineering Drawing MCQs with explanations · p.60

subject: Engineering Drawing
question: How many divisions a line has to be made if it is given to prepare plain scale up to 7 yards?
explanation: Whatever the representative factor may given, we just require number of units to divide the line in scale. Representative factor is only needed to find the length of the scale. Length of the scale = Representative fraction x Maximum length.
source: Engineering Drawing MCQs with explanations · p.61

subject: Engineering Drawing
question: What is the length of the scale, representative fraction given is 3/40 and maximum length to be represented in scale is 100 cm?
explanation: Length of the scale = Representative fraction x Maximum length. Length of the scale = 3/40 x 100 cm = 7.5 cm. That is to draw a scale for 100 cm with 3/40 R.F. We need to draw 7.5 cm length line and divide to 10 decimeters.
source: Engineering Drawing MCQs with explanations · p.61

subject: Engineering Drawing
question: In preparing a plain scale of feet and yards, the first division is to be divided into how many sub-divisions?
explanation: Given that the plain scale is to be made with feet and yards. Generally 1st part is divided into sub-divisions here is feet. We know 1 yard is equal to 3 feet, so 1st division should be divided into 3 sub-divisions.
source: Engineering Drawing MCQs with explanations · p.61

subject: Engineering Drawing
question: In preparing a plain scale of feet and inches, how many sub-divisions do the first division is to be divided?
explanation: Given that the plain scale is to be made with feet and inches. Generally 1st part is divided into sub-divisions here is inches. We know 1 feet is equal to 12 inches, so 1st division should be divided into 12 sub-divisions.
source: Engineering Drawing MCQs with explanations · p.62

subject: Engineering Drawing
question: In preparing a plain scale of miles and furlongs, how many divisions do the first part is to be made?
explanation: Given that the plain scale is to be made with miles and furlongs. Generally 1st part is divided into sub-divisions here is furlong. 1 mile is equal to 8 feet, so 1st division should be divided into 8 sub-divisions.
